name: walls-palette-32
description:
Interior tileset for indoor rooms — a 10x10 grid of 32x32 tiles, gids 4301-4400, where gid = firstgid + (row * 10 + col) and a tile's `position` is its PIXEL offset (col * 32, row * 32). All 100 cells are declared; 50 hold art and 50 are fully transparent and marked `unused_`.

FOUR COLOURS CARRY EVERYTHING. Dark #3A3A50 is outline. White #F8F8F8 is a wall's TOP surface, the part you see from above. Sage #9CA99E is a wall's SOUTH-FACING SIDE, drawn hanging below its cap and over the floor. Grey tile is FLOOR. So white-over-sage is a wall you see the front of, white alone is a wall seen only from above, and grey is where you walk.

TWO SHAPES BUILD EVERY WALL. A horizontal wall is a 12px CAP BAND — outline y0-1, white y2-9, outline y10-11 — and that band is the wall's footprint in plan. A vertical wall is a 14px STRIPE — outline, 10px white, outline — and which side of its cell the stripe hugs is how this sheet carries handedness: a stripe at x18-31 has floor to its east and so is a WEST wall, a stripe at x0-13 is an EAST wall. Mixing the two in one run makes a wall jump 18px mid-length, which is the same failure `outdoor-walls.json` documents outdoors.

A WALL'S HEIGHT IS DRAWN AS SEPARATE CELLS, and that is the one thing that makes this sheet different from `outdoor-walls.json` to use. Outdoors a wall's footprint and its height share a single cell, so its collider has to be the thin strip at its base — which is what makes it walk-behind, and what lets the player overlap its upper pixels. Here a north wall is a cap cell, then zero or more `face_fill` cells, then a `face_end` cell, and every one of them is wall through and through. So they block whole, none of them is walk-behind, and none needs to be: the cap always blocks before the player could reach a position north of a face.

The pieces fall into six families, named by their prefix. `wall_` is the room perimeter — runs, end caps and openings for all four sides. `face_` is the sage side hanging below a wall, in fill and terminating variants. `mass_` is a wall several cells thick in plan, with its own nine-slice edges. `pier_` is a free-standing interior wall, including the corners and T where one meets another. `floor_` is the walkable grey tile, plain plus grout-edge variants. `void_` is unlit space.

NOTE: these tiles are 32x32 while maps use tileSize 16. That is deliberate and must not be 'fixed' by re-slicing the art to 16x16 — the sheet is authored at 32.

walls-palette.description: The whole 10x10 sheet as one object, in grid order, so every cell's gid, key and pixel offset line up arithmetically and none can be forgotten. A tile's family is carried by its `name` prefix rather than by object grouping — see the sheet description.

walls-palette-0-1.name: wall_west_north_end
walls-palette-0-1.description: North end of a WEST wall. A vertical wall is a 14px stripe — outline, 10px of white top surface, outline — and which side of its cell the stripe hugs is how this sheet carries handedness. A stripe at x18-31 sits against floor to its EAST, so it is a WEST wall; a stripe at x0-13 is an EAST wall. Mixing the two in one run is what makes a wall jump 18px mid-length. The horizontal outline at y10-11 is a course seam, so a long run does not read as one extruded block. Collider is exactly the 14 columns the stripe covers, full height: a wall is crossed sideways, and a shorter box would leave a hole between rows.

Here the face begins in this same cell at y12-31 and continues into the cells below — see face_fill and face_end. Solid as a whole cell because the art covers the whole cell, and because nothing in this sheet ever lets the player stand north of a wall's side face — the cap above it always blocks first. That is why no tile here needs the base-strip walk-behind trick `outdoor-walls.json` relies on outdoors: there, a wall's height and footprint share one cell, so the player must be able to overlap its upper pixels. walls-palette-8-5.name: pier_north_cap
walls-palette-8-5.description: North cap of a free-standing interior wall — outline across y0-1 and down both edges, open at the bottom so it continues south. Pixel-identical to the cell at (6, 6). Solid as a whole cell because the art covers the whole cell, and because nothing in this sheet ever lets the player stand north of a wall's side face — the cap above it always blocks first. That is why no tile here needs the base-strip walk-behind trick `outdoor-walls.json` relies on outdoors: there, a wall's height and footprint share one cell, so the player must be able to overlap its upper pixels. Here a wall's height is drawn as SEPARATE cells, so each one is wall through and through.

walls-palette-4-6.name: wall_west_run_alt
walls-palette-4-6.description: WEST wall run — same 14px stripe at x18-31 as wall_west_run, with slightly different shading. A vertical wall is a 14px stripe — outline, 10px of white top surface, outline — and which side of its cell the stripe hugs is how this sheet carries handedness. A stripe at x18-31 sits against floor to its EAST, so it is a WEST wall; a stripe at x0-13 is an EAST wall. Mixing the two in one run is what makes a wall jump 18px mid-length.
